transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (Orchid Head of Platform), Devon Grant (CTO), Ravi Kumar (SRE), Sonia Park (Security)
---
Auto-summary (generated): Demo of rate/quotas and multi-tenant controls. Walkthrough of Console + API for org/project keys, priority tiers, and burst handling. Customer requested benchmarks and SOC2 docs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Arjun, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lena Torres: Doing good, thanks. Busy week but ready to go.
[00:09] Devon Grant: Yup, morning, afternoon, whatever time it is for you.
[00:13] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: we'll show the Console flows for org vs project keys, then Arjun will demo priority policies, siloed bursts, and then we'll cover security and next steps.
[00:21] Ravi Kumar: Sounds good. Our main thing — we want to make sure noisy tenants don't blow up latency for the rest of the platform.
[00:26] Sonia Park: And from security, I'm mainly here to confirm encryption, audit logs, and SSO integration.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Perfect — we'll hit those. Before we dive, can you remind us of your current setup? Where are you running models today?
[00:38] Lena Torres: We're hybrid. Most inference is on-proc with in-house GPUs for privacy, but we also use a managed endpoint for some consumer features. We're experimenting with offloading burst traffic to a hosted provider.
[00:48] Devon Grant: Our goals — keep P95 < 120ms for chat completions, cost targets are tight, and we need degredation strategies when capacity is constrained. Sorry, degraded not degredation —
[00:59] Maya Chen: No worries. Arjun, can you share your screen and we'll jump into the Console?
[01:03] Arjun Patel: Yep, sharing now. Let me know if screen's fuzzy.
[01:08] [screen share starts — Console view]
[01:10] Arjun Patel: So here is an org-level view. You can see projects underneath, each with its own API keys. We demonstrate policy inheritance — an org policy sets default quotas, and projects can override or opt into dedicated capacity.
[01:22] Devon Grant: Can project keys have separate billing and different quotas?
[01:25] Arjun Patel: Yes, billing attribution can be per-project and quotas are pluggable per project. You can set qps, token limits, concurrency. Also you can define priority tiers — let's show that.
[01:36] [00:01:40] Arjun Patel: Here is the priority policy editor. Teams can create tiers like "gold, silver, bronze". Each tier gets weight for fair-share scheduling, plus reserved headroom for high-priority keys.
[01:49] Lena Torres: So if a single customer goes berserk, they only consume their tier's slice?
[01:53] Arjun Patel: Exactly. We call that siloed burst — it's beneficial if you want predictable latency for a subset of tenants.
[01:59] Ravi Kumar: How's backpressure handled? Do you queue requests or reject?
[02:03] Arjun Patel: We have pluggable policies: soft queuing with retry hints, immediate 429 with informative headers, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants for graceful degradation.
[02:13] [02:15] Devon Grant: Is the fallback automatic across hosted/dedicated models?
[02:18] Arjun Patel: Yes, routing rules allow fallback to compatible model variants or different capacity pools based on policy priorities.
[02:23] Lena Torres: Any rough numbers on latency impact with those policies?
[02:26] Maya Chen: We can share benchmark numbers — in our recent tests, golden-tier requests stayed near baseline while bronze could see increased p95 under heavy load. We'll include detailed numbers in the follow-up.
[02:37] [02:40] Sonia Park: For security, do audit logs include per-request metadata, like which project key and which model was used?
[02:45] Arjun Patel: Yes, logs capture key, org, project, model id, latency, and token counts. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM or retained in Redwood for configurable retention windows.
[02:56] Sonia Park: And KMS for at-rest encryption?
[02:58] Arjun Patel: You can bring your own KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we integrate with managed KMS and can sign NDAs for key handling.
[03:07] [03:10] Devon Grant: Data residency — if we need EU-only, can you pin a model region?
[03:14] Maya Chen: Yes, routing can be region-constrained and we can provision Private deployments in your VPC or on-prem if needed.
[03:20] [03:22] Ravi Kumar: Hypothetical: if a bot suddenly spikes from a project, can burst be throttled to X qps for that key while others unaffected?
[03:30] Arjun Patel: Absolutely — you define a burst bucket per project. Example: project A has baseline 50 qps with burst up to 200 limited to a token budget per minute. Once consumed, they drop back.
[03:40] Devon Grant: Are those burst tokens shared across projects? We want to avoid noisy neighbor using org pool.
[03:44] Arjun Patel: You can isolate bursts per project or allow a shared org pool with fair-share. There are also priority-based preemption rules.
[03:51] [04:00] Speaker 1: Quick question — what's the experience for devs? How do they rotate keys?
[04:05] Maya Chen: Key rotation is available via the Console or API. You can issue project keys scoped to routes and set TTLs. SDKs support seamless rotation hooks.
[04:14] Lena Torres: How much of this is console-only vs API? We want infra-as-code.
[04:18] Arjun Patel: Everything is API-first. Console is a UX on top. We provide Terraform provider examples and SDK snippets.
[04:23] [04:30] Devon Grant: Pricing question — if we use org routing with priority tiers, is there an extra fee?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Pricing is primarily usage-based. There are enterprise add-ons for dedicated pools and advanced SLAs. We'll include org/project pricing scenarios in the follow-up doc.
[04:44] [04:50] Ravi Kumar: For the pilot, we want to validate P95 and also cost per 1m tokens under our traffic shape.
[04:55] Arjun Patel: Great, we'll send a benchmark checklist. Ideally you'll provide sample request traces or synthetic workloads.
[05:01] Lena Torres: We can provide anonymized traces. One more — how do you handle auditing for compliance?
[05:05] Sonia Park: (interrupting) SOC2 controls specifically.
[05:07] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II for the hosted product; Private customers can have additional attestations and a separate audit engagement. We'll share the security pack.
[05:15] [05:20] Arjun Patel: Demoing a policy change now — I'm lowering the bronze tier qps and adding a reserved headroom to gold. Apply changes — you can see that routing immediately recalculates and shows projected impact.
[05:34] [05:40] Devon Grant: Can we test this live with a canary?
[05:43] Arjun Patel: Yes, rollout controls allow canary percentages, and you can pin specific projects to testers before global rollout.
[05:50] Lena Torres: What happens if a fallback triggers to a cheaper model and the quality drops? Any evals for regressions?
[05:57] Arjun Patel: Redwood Optimize ties into quality monitoring — you can attach eval prompt sets and alerts if output regressions exceed thresholds. That ties into rollback policies.
[06:07] [06:10] Ravi Kumar: Ok, timeline-wise, we'd like to run a 2-week pilot and then decide on dedicated vs hosted in July. Is that realistic?
[06:18] Maya Chen: Totally realistic. We often run 2-week pilots with benchmarks and a go/no-go decision.
[06:23] Devon Grant: What's required from our side to start pilot?
[06:26] Arjun Patel: We'll need sample traces, target qps, a list of projects to include, and security contact for paperwork. We'll provide a spreadsheet template.
[06:34] [06:40] Sonia Park: I'll need the network diagram and SOC2 docs. We will also want the contract redlined by legal.
[06:45] Maya Chen: We'll get that across.
[06:47] [06:50] (slight crosstalk)
[06:53] Maya Chen: Any more objections or concerns?
[06:56] Devon Grant: I'm slightly worried about long-tail costs if we misconfigure burst buckets. How do we safeguard against that?
[07:03] Arjun Patel: You can set hard caps and anomaly alerts. Billing alerts can also pause a project's capacity if spend thresholds are hit.
[07:11] Lena Torres: Also we need RBAC so product teams can't change org-level policies.
[07:15] Arjun Patel: RBAC is implemented — roles for org admin, billing, project owner, and read-only.
[07:20] [07:30] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing scenarios and SOC2/network docs; Arjun will send benchmark checklist; Sonia will review security pack; Lena will confirm pilot scope.
[07:39] Devon Grant: Sounds good.
[07:41] Ravi Kumar: We'll aim to have traces ready by next week.
[07:43] Maya Chen: Great — any final quick questions?
[07:46] Sonia Park: One small one — do logs contain token-level content? We need to ensure PII isn't stored.
[07:51] Arjun Patel: By default Redwood logs metadata only. Full request bodies can be disabled; for pilot we'll ensure PII is redacted and you can opt into not storing prompt text.
[07:59] Lena Torres: That's important for us.
[08:02] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed pilot plan.
[08:06] Devon Grant: Appreciate it.
[08:08] Maya Chen: End of meeting.
